properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/26/2024 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Nicholson Township, Fayette county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/26/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8209586
Permit API: 051-23812
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/26/2024
Comments: On November 26, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a referral from OGI Charles Reaggle (IR 3864611 on 10/18/2024). OGI Charles Reaggle requested that a WQS follow up because of observed fluid dripping from both annulus wings. Well appears to be equipped for production. Site is well vegetated.Well tag requirement fulfilled with API number present on production tank. Well posting for Big Dog Energy does not appear to be correct Operator. In IR 3864611, the Department noted that the well transferred Operators from Big Dog Energy to Dorso LP, however the well has since transferred again to Apollo Resources as of October 30, 2024. The Department recommends Apollo Resources fulfill the well posting requirement in accordance with OGA3211(G).Drip still observed coming from the annulus. Specific conductivity was measured inside the annulus (7.62 mS / 7,620 uS), in the soil below the annulus (1.161 mS / 1,161 uS), and three background points of the soil surrounding the site (0.1805 mS / 180.5 uS), (0.1524 mS / 152.4 uS), (0.262 mS / 262 uS). These measurements of specific conductivity indicate that a release of brine has occurred from the annulus. The Department recommends the Operator repair the annulus to prevent further release. The Department recommends the Operator remove all impacted soil/material and properly disposing of the soil/material.Production tank on site and appears to be structurally sound at this time. Violations are being issued for release of production fluid to the ground. Previously issued violations in IR 3864611 by OGI Charles Reaggle are being evaluated under enforcement ID 435756.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 5th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Tyler Sites and Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 10:45 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 369107 dated 12/30/2022.A complaint was emailed to the Department regarding a tank overflow of produced fluid from the 100bbl steel storage tank onsite.Upon arriving at the site, produced fluid was observed on the side of the tank, tank steps, and pooled within the earthen dike. Oil product was also observed to be on the side of the 50bbl poly tank and around the thief hatch of the tank. It appears that the 100bbl steel tank had overflowed and released approximately 15-20 gallons of produced fluid to the ground within the earthen dike. It appears that an unknown amount of fluid (oil) was scrapped up and put into the 50bbl poly tank. The released fluids were contained to the earthen dike.The operator was contacted via phone while still onsite. The operator was unaware of the extent of the release. It was stated that a small release of 1 gallon was reported internally and a claim that everything was cleaned up. Since the release was being contained to the earthen dike, the operator stated that a cleanup crew would be onsite first thing in the morning to cleanup the release.1/4/2022 (11:00am)I stopped at the site and visual cleanup operations were nearly complete. The impacted area within the dike was scrapped up with an excavator and placed into a dump truck. Fresh clean gravel was onsite to reclaim the inside of the earthen dike. The impacted material will be hauled to their shop for future disposal.A follow-up inspection will be conducted by the Department once cleanup is completed.Violations are cited.

Violation ID: 999500
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 6/22/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator is having a rig drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run will take place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. Today's operations: Bull Run Rig 118 tagged cement at 315' and drilled with a 4" coring bit to a depth of 340'.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XTO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/09/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 994370
Permit API: 035-21217
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/09/2023
Comments: On May 9, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline followed up on a reported spill of production fluid from a tanker truck at the XTO Energy PA Tract Pad A. The spill occurred on 9 different areas of Dry Run Rd. and the short access road to Well Pad A. The volume of the spill is unknown. DEP spoke with Jason Canose with XTO on the phone and he said he would notify DEP when the tanker truck off loads. XTO would have a better estimate of a volume after this occurs. The spills along Dry Run Rd. occurred early on May 9, 2023. The cause of the spill from the tanker truck is suspected to be an open scrubber valve on the tanker truck. XTO was still investigating the cause of the spill during the DEP follow up to the incident. The size of the spills along the short access road and Dry Run Rd. varied in size from approximately 140 ft. x 8 ft. to 15 ft. x 10 in. DEP and XTO delineated and marked the 9 different spill areas for XTO contractors to begin excavating the impacted soil. DEP screened the 9 different spill areas with a soil conductivity meter and all the spill areas had sections of the individual areas where the conductivity was over range of the meter. The upper limit of DEP's soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The 9 spill areas were mostly contained to the road surface. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA GEN ENERGY CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/17/2022
Violation Code: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 972185
Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/17/2022
Comments: EPA Mechanical Integrity Test was conducted on 10/12/2022 at 09:58. Tubing pressure at commencement of test was 2225 p.s.i. Tubing annulus was filled with freshwater and pressured up to 800 p.s.i. MIT concluded at 10:28. Final pressure on tubing annuls was 800 p.s.i. Final pressure on tubing was 2225 p.s.i. Annulus of surface casing was monitored while the pressure test was underway, for any changes in the rate of bubbling. There were no abnormalities observed, indicating there is zonal isolation between the downhole injection zone, and the top-hole freshwater protection zones. The well has passed EPA's mechanical integrity test. PGE's remediation plan proposes the use of a resin material, with gas blocking capabilities. The resin will be pumped into the annular space of the surface casing at a depth of approximately 350', or the cap rock nearest this depth. This depth is determined to be below the deepest fresh groundwater in the area. It is anticipated that by placing the resin at this depth, the cap rock will be restored, thereby preventing the gas from permeating the micro-annulus that is allowing the gas to flow to surface. The resin has been used in similar annular gas scenarios, with success. An alternative procedure of pumping cement into the annular space has been discussed, but the outcome of this procedure is often times unpredictable, and could leave the casing integrity in a compromised condition. PGE anticipates that the resin will be available to them in April, of 2023. The product is currently in short supply, and the available stock has been allotted to other customers.

Violation ID: 902028
Permit API: 125-28620
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington

Inspection Date: 12/10/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/10/2020 at approximately 2:15 PM. The operator reported that an open top buster tank overflowed during flow back operations and approximately 20 gallons impacted the ground behind the tank. The operator reported a total of approximately 188 gallons total was spilled, with 168 gallons spilling to secondary containment. The operator is reporting that the spill will be remediated in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1). Nate Smiell and Brandon Carson with Range are on site, on my arrival. The following is observed: The site is currently in flowback operations (Photo 1). The pad drain has been closed. According to Mr. Smiell, he identified the spill at approximately 12:15 PM on 12/10/2020 during a routine inspection of the site. A time for the incident could not be provided at the time of this inspection. Mr. Smiell stated that it could have occurred anywhere between 12 and 24 hours prior to it being found. According to Mr. Smiell the open top tanks are to be inspected and the contents measured every hour. The Department requests these inspection logs be provided for the 24 hours preceding when it was found. Additionally, the Department requests the secondary containment logs for the past month, and at what time was the secondary containment remediated with the vacuum truck? Mr. Carson stated that it was possible that on-site cameras may have recorded the incident. The Department requests more information on this, whether they were able to record the incident and at what time the incident occurred if it was recorded. SPSI is on site and prepping to begin remediation of the site impacted by the spill. The Department requests photographs of the site post clean up as well as the waste manifest once it becomes available. The Department recommended to Mr. Smiell that the operator increase the length of the secondary containment (Photo 2 & 6). Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, more violations may be forthcoming.

Permit API: 123-42131
Unconventional: No
County: Warren

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/01/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, corrosion, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. NO methane was detected in the slam bar holes utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023. Pressures observed at the time of inspection were: 1psi on the 6-5/8"x2" annulus and 48psi on the inside of the 2" tubing. This well was labeled with an incorrect well API#, this issue was brought to the attention of the operator and promptly fixed. Further inspections of this well may be warranted to determine the root cause of the complaint.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/14/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8275341
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8189996
Permit API: 081-21945
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. The EC of the fluid present in the trench along the southeast edge of the well head secondary containment was between 4.03 mS/cm and 5.06 mS/cm. The 30 ft by 50 ft area of the pad surface reported to have been impacted by the release southeast of the well heads had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 2.48 mS/cm and 4.00 mS/cm. A vaccum truck was sucking up fluid from the impacted area of the pad surface during this inspection. Other areas of the pad surface had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 856 uS/cm to 1990 uS/cm. According to the company man, excavation of this area was going to be completed by Tobias Machining, present on site during this inspection, and characterization of the site would be conducted by Penn E and R who was en-route to the site during this inspection. The Department requests a justification for the estimated release volume. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up fluid with elevated EC from the pad surface. Violations noted against permit 081-21945 for the 6/6/24 reported release. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the 5/8/24 release discovered by the Department. These violations will be closed upon attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On 04/09/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and sunny. Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey and I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The DEP was unable to field measure the Electrical Conductivity (EC) at the release point due to stimulation activities. The EC of the fluids up-gradient of the stormwater basin were ~ 240 us/cm (photo #3). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-529) UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the discharge the EC of the fluids were 71 us/cm (photo #13). The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-530) from UNT Rockwell Creek downstream of the discharge the EC of fluids were ~160 us/cm. As of 04/06/2026 5,293 barrels (166,729 gallons) have been recovered onsite. Resource management will continue screening and sampling ten monitoring points twice a week. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

Violation ID: 851804
Permit API: 051-23818
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-05-31
Comments: On 5/31/19 a follow up inspection of the Waters 10 Well Site was conducted accompanied by WQS Supervisor John Carson in response to issues noted in a prior inspection. The following was observed: >>The well equipment and site appeared unchanged from the previous inspection. >>The production/brine tank remained in poor condition with visible seepage from the rust holes in the tanks lower end. In response to the initial inspection the operator stated that the tank had not been used and that the well produced no brine. At the time of the inspection the tank held roughly 10-20" of cloudy fluid and dead vegetation on the earth work around it indicated a ground plume of contamination. This piece of equipment can no longer serve as a tank or appropriate storage device for production fluids. Immediate replacement of failed equipment and removal of impacted materials recommended. This constitutes a violation of SWMA 401(A), 610(4), 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, and 25 Pa. Code § 78.57(a) in that the operator failed to store hazardous waste in accordance with the rules and regulations of the DEP resulting in conditions hazardous to public health and safety and a failure to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. A site characterization is necessary to assess the extent of impact and appropriate action to remedy contamination. >>Gravel and other debris remained sloughed onto the public roadway and continue to indicate substantial runoff from the site during rain events. This constitutes a violation of 25 Pa. Code 102.11(a)(1) in that the operator failed to successfully design, implement, and maintain site BMPs.

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8211209
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: On 12/17/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 45F and sunny. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Hydraulic fracturing activities remain ongoing onsite and are estimated to be completed near the end of next week. Equipment to support well stimulation remain onsite and all equipment which is required to be held in containment was observed in secondary containment structures (photos #2-6)This inspection was conducted in response to a release of produced fluids from secondary containment reported by Greylock on 12/13/2024 at 0245 hours (CTS #385788). The cause of the release was determined to be a hydraulic fracturing pump which leaked produced fluids that accumulated and overtopped from secondary containment; the release has been contained. Contaminated material was already removed and backfilled by my arrival onsite (photo #7). The soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~40us/cm. Standing fluids were observed near the area of the release and field measured for EC at ~1140us/cm. Two vacuum trucks for removing fluids have been stationed onsite and were sent to remove the fluids from this area. Greylock took corrective action after this release and rebuilt the entire containment berm and rig-matting system with an 18-inch wall for increased capacity and to prevent additional releases (photo #8).The low points of the produced fluids offload containment structure which was the site of the release on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) have been repaired and a pump has been installed to continuously remove fluids from this containment structure as they accumulate (photos #9-11).The drainage system which was conveying fluids and diesel into the site's infiltration basin on 12/09/2024 (Inspection Report #3881391) remains shut in and a pump has been installed to remove accumulating fluids. No fluids were observed entering the basin at the time of this inspection (photo #12). Contaminated materials have not yet been excavated from the basin as per my previous recommendation to follow Act 2 remediation guidelines (photo #13).The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to remove fluids as they accumulate in secondary containment structures.-Continue following Act 2 remediation requirements for the ongoing remediation efforts onsite, including those set to take place in the infiltration basin.-Continuing daily secondary containment inspection.No additional violations noted at this time. The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

A wooden pallet was observed floating within the high level of water within the production tanks secondary containment and vegetation was observed to be growing all through the containment as well. During IR 3488331, the Department recommended the Operator keep all secondary containments dry and prevent the growth of vegetation within them. As the observations in IR 3488331 appear to be similar and/or unchanged from today's inspection, it does not appear that the Operator is maintaining the storage capacity of the secondary containment. Along the perimeter of the well pad, black tubing was observed laying on the ground, the Department is recommending the Operator remove all production equipment not currently in use. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued for the production tanks insufficient holding capacity and future violations may be forthcoming for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use.

Report Details

Permit API: 125-29122

Comments: On November 7, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Burkett well site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. This inspection was conducted in response to Stimulation notifications that were submitted by the operator on October 31, 2025. Stimulation operations were scheduled to begin on November 4, 2025, for wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated for this site on August 12, 2020.The following was observed during this inspection:Upon starting this inspection, the Department spoke with Halliburton representative Phillip Gonzalez, who cautioned the Department about the hazards present on site, such as moving vehicles and high-pressure lines. Wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H appear to be undergoing stimulation operations simultaneously at the time of inspection (photos 8 and 9). Five additional well heads are onsite that appear to be in production (photo 7).The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 15). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 16). All other containers and machinery onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 2 and 10). The well pad containment appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no tears observed. Range Resources representative Justin Fedor was onsite during this inspection who provided the secondary containment inspection log upon request (photo 11). No evidence of fluid leaks was observed from the portion of the MCC Partners to Burkett Temporary Waterline (TWL) at the well pad (photo 12). The Act 9 sign is located at the access road entrance and is not obscured from vegetation, in accordance with 78a55 requirements (photo 24). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness and Contingency (PPC) plan, well permits, and safety data sheets are located onsite (photos 17-20). However, the PPC plan is not specific to this site. The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. The access road and well pad were muddy during this inspection with little observable gravel (photos 1 and 23). This appears to be causing sedimentation from the access road to occur in the rock-lined channel along the access road (photos 21 and 22). This sedimentation appears to continue downslope for approximately 20 feet along the access road and stops within the boundaries of the well site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the accumulating sediment from the access road in the rock-lined channel.Violations are to be issued in IR 4091983 for failure to have a site-specific PPC plan on site and for failure to maintain the access road which resulted in sedimentation.

Comments: This is a producing combination well with a gas powered pumpjack attached. The well is plumbed to a 210 barrel stock tank and 50 barrel poly tank on site. It appears as though there has been a leak on this site recently. There is an area approximately 10x20 feet with staining of soil and dead vegetation, along with a finger of oil stained soil in an erosion rill about 20 feet further. The estimated volume released is unknown but appears to be less than a barrel. The operator was contacted regarding this issue and potential cleanup. The operator brought in a treatment system that removed the paraffin from the well. Some was put into the drums on site or otherwise leaked and was not cleaned up. By the end of the day on 8/23, the operator had the site cleaned up and seeded and mulched. No further inspection of this site will be necessary at this time.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4160648 where violations were issued for heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release. The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4181625.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release.Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead, IR 4181625 documents the Department's request for OGI assistance to assess the integrity of the gas wellhead. While on site, the Department called Matt Anderson (listed as Managing Member in the Departments records for Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc), to notify them about the potential gas leak, however, Mr. Anderson stated he no longer manages Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc and provided the Department with an email address for Oil and gas Mgmt Inc. The Department then attempted to contact Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc again by calling the number on the well tag, however, this number was out of service. Violations are also being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate Operator information posted on site. Based on today's inspection, violations are being continued at this time for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release and new violations are being issued for failure to have updated and accurate operator information on site.
